entries.definition: Producing the same result regardless of how many times applied.
entries.non_ste_example: You can hit DELETE as many times as you want and it won't break anything.

entries.definition: Not able to be changed after creation.
entries.ste_example: The configuration object is immutable after initialization.
entries.non_ste_example: Once you set the config, you can't mess with it anymore.

entries.definition: Executing as a single unit that either fully completes or fully fails.
entries.non_ste_example: The DB update either all goes through or none of it does.

entries.definition: Executing without blocking the main program flow.
entries.non_ste_example: The handler runs in the background so nothing gets stuck waiting.

entries.definition: Always producing the same output for the same input.
entries.non_ste_example: The hash always spits out the same thing for the same input.

entries.definition: Not storing information between requests or operations.
entries.non_ste_example: The gateway doesn't remember anything between requests.

entries.definition: Continuing to exist after the program or system restarts.
entries.ste_example: The session data is persistent across server restarts.
entries.non_ste_example: Your session sticks around even if the server reboots.

entries.definition: Referring to or calling itself during execution.
entries.ste_example: The directory walk function is recursive.
entries.non_ste_example: The function calls itself over and over to dig through folders.

entries.definition: Allowed to contain a null or undefined value.
entries.non_ste_example: Email can be null if the user didn't give one.

entries.definition: Still available but no longer recommended for use. Will be removed in a future version.
entries.ste_example: The v1 endpoint is deprecated. Use the v2 endpoint.
entries.non_ste_example: Don't use the old v1 stuff — it's gonna be gone soon.
